home.title: The App Fair Project
home.tagline: The free and open-source app store for the iPhone and Android
home.intro1: The App Fair Project is a non-profit charitable organization dedicated to the creation of mobile software applications for the public good. The project was founded in 2022 as a worldwide nexus for free apps to be built, distributed, and maintained.
home.intro2: App Fair apps are free to download and use. They contain no advertising or tracking software. Donations and grants pay for development and distribution.

stores.heading: Install from the store you already use
stores.body: The App Fair reviews each release before publishing it to the App Store and Google Play. Distribution through F-Droid and AltStore is planned.

features.heading: What to expect from our apps

items.title: Free and open source
items.body: You can read, modify, and redistribute the source code for every App Fair app under its free software license.

items.title: Advertising
items.body: App Fair apps contain no ads or advertising SDKs.

items.title: App stores
items.body: Install apps from the Apple App Store or Google Play. F-Droid and AltStore distribution is planned.

items.title: Free to use
items.body: All app features are available without payment. Apps cannot charge for subscriptions, in-app purchases, or upgrades.

items.title: Funding
items.body: Donations and grants fund the apps and their distribution. The App Fair is a nonprofit.

items.title: Privacy
items.body: Apps cannot collect analytics or tracking data. Permissions and network access must serve a stated app feature.

cornerstones.heading: How we build apps
cornerstones.lead: We publish the code, support iOS and Android, and build translation and accessibility support into the apps.

items.title: Public source
items.body: The source code, build configuration, and dependencies are available under free and open-source licenses.

items.title: iOS and Android
items.body: Each app uses a shared codebase to provide the same features in native iOS and Android apps.

items.title: Translation
items.body: App text is stored in translation files. Translations cover the app and its store listing.

items.title: Accessibility
items.body: Apps must support screen readers, large text sizes, and switch control, with sufficient color contrast.

how.heading: From source code to the app stores

steps.title: Develop the app
steps.body: Developers publish the app’s source under GPL-2.0-or-later. Every dependency must have public source under a compatible free-software license.

steps.title: Submit a release
steps.body: The developer submits each release to the App Fair for review against the inclusion criteria.

steps.title: Publish to the stores
steps.body: The App Fair submits approved releases to the App Store and Google Play. Each store also reviews the app before publication.

how.note: The App Fair builds each release and compares it with the developer's published build before accepting it.

cta.heading: Help fund the apps
cta.body: Your donation pays for app development, release review, and the servers that host the catalog.

free.text: App Fair apps are free to use and respect the {freedoms}.
free.freedomsLabel: four essential freedoms of free software

noAds.text: App Fair apps contain no ads or advertising SDKs.

openSource.text: The source code for each app and its dependencies is public. You can inspect, modify, and redistribute it under its free software licenses.

noTracking.text: App Fair apps cannot collect analytics or tracking data. Permissions and network access must serve a stated app feature.
